models.title: Prescribed drug mass from a supplied body-surface-area basis
models.summary: Multiplies a supplied body surface area by an independently authorized mass-per-area amount for one administration. This does not compute a root-based body-area estimate or select a regimen.

relationship.original_equation: Client size (body surface area) x Order (mass per area) = Dose (mass)
relationship.locator: Pharmacology for Nurses, 2.4 Dosage Calculations, Body Surface Area Method, example step3 and final displayed Client size x Order = Dose
relationship.translation_notes: Introduced A,d,D map to supplied client BSA, ordered mass per area, and resulting mass. Use A in m^2, d in kg/m^2 and D in kg; dimensions (M L^-2)*L^2=M. Input d and output D share kg's runtime scale, so d*A is canonical without a mg conversion factor. The earlier square-root BSA step is excluded entirely; A is an external quantity with its own provenance. Use only the source's step3 mass result1.34 mg from2 mg/m^2 and already reported0.67 m^2. Its later dimensional-analysis line incorrectly labels the mass product as mL; that line is not the authority. This area-normalized prescription has a different normalization quantity/dimensions from mass-per-body-mass prescription; a kg-to-m^2 unit conversion cannot turn one into the other.

variables.context: Same patient, independently supplied body surface area and already authorized active-drug mass per body surface area for one administration. assumptions: Source arithmetic: multiply patient area by the ordered mass-per-area amount; example step3 explicitly gives a mass result.
Application profile: A is supplied independently and the per-administration coefficient is already clinically qualified for the patient. This definition is not drug-specific population validation.
Assignment scope: root-based BSA estimation remains deferred. The model does not reconstruct A or infer a dose coefficient.
limitations: Does not establish drug selection, per-day frequency, dose limits, rounded tablet quantities, renal adjustment or BSA method validity.
A percentage of an adult reference dose, a per-weight amount and a mass-per-area prescription are distinct conventions and cannot be substituted by a unit label.
The source's numerical regimen is pedagogical only; it is not promoted to a reusable recommendation or default.

models.title: Calculated mid-upper-arm muscle circumference under circular geometry
models.summary: Subtracts pi times triceps skinfold thickness from total upper-arm circumference to estimate the inner muscle-core circumference under a circular, uniform-rim model. No total muscle mass, sarcopenia diagnosis or risk threshold is inferred.

relationship.locator: Principles of Nutritional Assessment: Body Composition,11.2.2, Calculation of mid-upper-arm-muscle circumference; shared geometric assumptions in11.1.4
relationship.translation_notes: Introduced C,T,M map to MUAC,TSK,MUAMC. Both measurements and output use metres, so cm/mm scales cancel without an inline conversion factor. Dimensions L-(1*L)=L. Source pi is serialized as3.141592653589793, a local floating-point approximation to the mathematical constant, not a fitted clinical parameter. The source derives the inner-circle circumference by subtracting the diameter decrement represented by a doubled fat-layer skinfold. Under this geometry C>pi*T ensures positive inner diameter, hence the feasibility guard; it is not a clinical cutoff. The source's model ignores variable skinfold compressibility and fat nonuniformity. Its central bone core is enclosed, not removed. BAPEN's3.14 coefficient is a rounded alternative source view of the same relationship, not another model.

variables.definition: Total measured circumference at the declared mid-upper-arm site.
variables.context: Same human mid-upper arm, assessment side/site and measurement state; paired MUAC and triceps skinfold thickness. Conditional circular-section/uniform-fat-rim geometry; a positive nondegenerate inner muscle-and-bone core is required. This geometric anthropometric proxy has no universal age/sex/ethnic clinical validation or percentile mapping in this record.
variables.domain: Finite strictly positive and greater than pi*T for the model's nondegenerate inner core.

constants.meaning: Local floating-point approximation to source mathematical pi; not a fitted clinical coefficient

assumptions: Source geometric assumptions: circular/cylindrical limb approximation, uniform surrounding fat rim, doubled-fold representation, and ignored variation in skinfold compressibility.
Application profile: same arm/site/state measurements and a nondegenerate positive inner core. The definition is conditional geometry, not a population-fitted muscle-mass prediction.
Source notes historical/community and elderly proxy uses; those uses do not establish universal clinical classification validity for this record.
limitations: Nonuniform fat, noncircular shape, skinfold compressibility and individual humerus proportion can bias the proxy; these are not corrected here.
One-dimensional circumference is not muscle area or volume and can be insensitive to small muscle-mass changes. No percentage, percentile, diagnosis or intervention is returned.
Zero fold thickness is not admitted as a measured human fold in this profile; an ideal zero-rim limit is mathematically M=C but is not claimed as a valid clinical observation.

models.inverse_notes: Target C: known M>0,T>0 give C=M+pi*T>0 and automatically satisfy inner-core feasibility. Target T: known C>0,M>0 with C>M give T=(C-M)/pi>0; pi is fixed positive, not a freely solvable input. Retain source geometry and measurement context. Check M=0.25132741228718347 m,T=0.02 m gives C=0.3141592653589793 m and forward M matches; solving T from that C,M gives0.02 m. If M=C, T=0 would follow but is outside this measured-fold profile; M>C would require negative fold. M=0 would be a degenerate inner core and violates the declared feasibility guard. No muscle-mass or biological causal inversion is asserted.
